scope: Mission Control integration: integrate the progress-heartbeat (d86774d) and secretless-reconciliation (b050075) candidates, add the owner-authenticated fleet-watch capability POST /api/fleet-supervisor/:projectId, then restore the AskRigor fleet watch through the control plane and resume A19-A20. No token extraction, no second scheduler, no replay of crossed source-review requests.

findings_2026_09_24.askrigor_watch: Live /snapshot (primary daemon, 17:40Z) lists all fleet watches unfiltered: only project:human-design and project:mission-control. No AskRigor watch ever existed centrally; the earlier 'hourly watch re-enabled' checkpoint most likely referred to the external hourly fallback. The daemon mutation can only reconfigure an existing watch.
findings_2026_09_24.askrigor_project_identity: No project:askrigor (or any AskRigor project id) exists in central state; only task:askrigor-system-alignment. Watches are enrolled only by work_queue_published with nonterminal items, which AskRigor never published centrally.
findings_2026_09_24.classifier_consequence: Worker askrigor-system-alignment projects progress.outcomeAdvancement=UNKNOWN, so classifyFleetSupervisorTick returns PROJECT_INTEGRITY_FAILURE (stop + notify owner) before the WORKER_DIRECTIVE_CONTINUITY_GAP branch. An enrolled watch would therefore not route A19-A20 to mc-project-manager as the handoff expected.
findings_2026_09_24.status: Owner decision needed on how AskRigor obtains its A19-A20 directive; see the Claude session report.
